title: Take component side, layer, type, suffix and weight from one canonical catalog entry

facts.note: Task text about deriving components, naming file patterns, estimating effort, or editing the catalog. Bare 'wagon'/'WMBT' is not enough on its own; it must co-occur with one of these catalog-related terms.
Needs an observer that knows the agent is authoring plans/wagons/WMBTs/docs rather than coding.

values: component side/layer/type/URN, file pattern or weight added or changed in a plan artifact
facts.note: Diff-level detection of component entries in plan files, or of edits to the catalog itself.

values: component values not from one matching catalog entry
catalog type missing suffix/description/weight or out of sync with coder conventions
facts.note: The validator checks the catalog; checking plan entries against it is reviewer-judged until a plan-schema detector exists.

fires: Planner derives the components a feature needs and assigns side, layer and type.
Planner writes a component URN (its side/layer values) into a plan, WMBT or doc.
Planner states the expected file name pattern for a planned component in a given language.
Planner estimates effort/footprint using component complexity weights.
The component type catalog itself is added to, edited or validated.
doesNotFire: Coder implementing an already-planned component (coder backend/frontend conventions govern).
Planning text that names no components, types, file patterns or weights (e.g. pure acceptance wording).
Docs unrelated to component derivation, file patterns, effort estimation or the catalog.

given: A plan, WMBT or doc derives components, names file patterns or estimates effort, or the catalog is edited. The catalog (context.component-type-catalog) lists every type by side, layer, per-language suffix, description and weight, derived from the coder backend/frontend conventions.
when: You set a component's side, layer, type, URN side/layer, file pattern or weight.
then: Take all of a component's values from one matching catalog entry: side, layer, type, the target language's suffix and the weight.
prefer: Take URN side/layer values from the catalog structure; look entries up by side.layer.type.
Pick the type whose description fits; estimate effort with catalog weights.
Catalog edits: keep each type complete and derived from coder conventions; flag mismatches, never pick ad hoc.
avoid: Ad-hoc types, layers, sides or weights; tweaking weights to shape an estimate.
Mixing values across entries or languages.
why: One canonical catalog keeps component derivation and effort estimates consistent with the coder conventions instead of ad hoc.
evidence: Every planned component's side, layer and type resolve to exactly one entry in context.component-type-catalog.
Each declared file pattern equals that same entry's suffix for the component's language (an entry with no suffix for that language means the type is unavailable there).
Each weight used in effort/footprint estimation equals that same entry's weight.

Catalog examples: backend.integration.engines → *_engine.py, weight 3 (highest complexity); backend.presentation.routes → *_routes.py, weight 0; frontend.presentation.controllers → *_bloc.dart / *-store.ts, weight 2.
verifier_detail: Resolve each plan component by the tuple (side, layer, type, language) against context.component-type-catalog; suffix and weight must come from that single tuple, not merely exist somewhere in the catalog.

Suffix collisions — resolve by side/layer, never by suffix alone: frontend.presentation.controllers and frontend.integration.stores both use typescript '*-store.ts'; domain entities use catch-all '*.py'/'*.ts'/'*.dart' and backend value_objects also accept '*.py'; frontend components use catch-all '*.tsx'; backend.integration.stores ('*-store.ts') shares the TypeScript suffix too.

Multi-suffix entries: backend application ports python 'protocols.py, *_port.py'; backend workflows python '*_workflow.py, *_saga.py'; backend value_objects python '*_vo.py, *.py' — any listed alternative is valid.
Language-missing entries (TypeScript only): frontend presentation containers, hooks, directives, filters; frontend integration workers.
The source prescribes no aggregation formula for weights; do not flag an estimate for how weights are combined, only for weights that differ from the matching entry.

sharedNodes.text:
CANONICAL COMPONENT TYPE CATALOG. Enumerates every component type by side (backend|frontend), layer, file suffix per language, description and complexity weight; derived from the coder backend/frontend conventions (.claude/conventions/coder/{backend,frontend}.convention.yaml). Entries are listed under side.layer headings; side.layer.type is the lookup key for an entry. Format: type — suffix(es) — description — weight. Types without a suffix for a language are not available in that language.

BACKEND (term backend_catalog, 'Backend component types': all backend component types keyed by layer (presentation, application, domain, integration), each with per-language file suffix, description, and complexity weight). Languages: python | typescript.
backend.presentation:
- controllers — *_controller.py | *-controller.ts — Request/response handlers for external interfaces — 1
- routes — *_routes.py | *-routes.ts — Routing configuration and endpoint definitions — 0
- serializers — *_serializer.py | *-serializer.ts — Input/output data serialization and formatting — 0.5
- validators — *_validator.py | *-validator.ts — Input validation at the edge — 0.5
- middleware — *_middleware.py | *-middleware.ts — Cross-cutting request/response processing — 1
- guards — *_guard.py | *-guard.ts — Authentication and authorization at transport layer — 1
- views — *_view.py | *-view.ts — Server-side rendered templates and UI components — 1
backend.application:
- use_cases — *_use_case.py | *-use-case.ts — Application-specific business workflows — 2
- handlers — *_handler.py | *-handler.ts — Command, query, and event processing — 1
- ports — protocols.py, *_port.py | *-port.ts — Interfaces and protocols for integration layer — 0
- dtos — *_dto.py | *-dto.ts — Data transfer objects between layers — 0
- policies — *_policy.py | *-policy.ts — Application-level business policies and rules — 1
- workflows — *_workflow.py, *_saga.py | *-workflow.ts — Long-running processes and orchestrations — 2
backend.domain:
- entities — *.py | *.ts — Core business objects with identity and lifecycle — 1
- value_objects — *_vo.py, *.py | *-vo.ts — Immutable types with equality-by-value semantics — 0.5
- aggregates — *_aggregate.py | *-aggregate.ts — Transactional consistency boundaries — 2
- services — *_service.py | *-service.ts — Domain services for cross-entity business logic — 1
- specifications — *_spec.py | *-spec.ts — Composable business rules and predicates — 0.5
- events — *_event.py | *-event.ts — Domain events representing facts that happened — 0
- exceptions — *_exception.py | *-exception.ts — Domain-specific errors and invariant violations — 0
backend.integration:
- repositories — *_repository.py | *-repository.ts — Data persistence and retrieval adapters — 2
- clients — *_client.py | *-client.ts — External API and service clients — 1
- caches — *_cache.py | *-cache.ts — Caching implementations — 0.5
- engines — *_engine.py | *-engine.ts — Computational and processing engines (ML, graph, optimization) — 3
- formatters — *_formatter.py | *-formatter.ts — Output formatting and rendering services — 1
- notifiers — *_notifier.py | *-notifier.ts — Communication and notification services — 1
- queues — *_queue.py | *-queue.ts — Message queue and event streaming clients — 2
- stores — *_store.py | *-store.ts — File and object storage adapters — 1
- mappers — *_mapper.py | *-mapper.ts — Data transformation and mapping between layers — 0.5
- schedulers — *_scheduler.py | *-scheduler.ts — Background tasks and scheduled jobs — 2
- monitors — *_monitor.py | *-monitor.ts — Observability and infrastructure monitoring — 1

FRONTEND (term frontend_catalog, 'Frontend component types': all frontend component types keyed by layer (presentation, application, domain, integration), each with per-language file suffix, description, and complexity weight). Languages: dart | typescript.
frontend.presentation:
- views — *_page.dart | *-page.tsx — Full-screen views and pages — 1
- components — *_widget.dart | *.tsx — Reusable UI components — 0.5
- containers — (no dart) | *-container.tsx — Smart components connected to state — 1
- controllers — *_bloc.dart | *-store.ts — UI state management and business logic — 2
- routes — *_router.dart | *-routes.ts — Navigation and routing configuration — 0
- layouts — *_layout.dart | *-layout.tsx — Page structure and composition templates — 1
- styles — *_theme.dart | *.css — Design tokens, themes, and styling — 0
- animations — *_animation.dart | *-animation.ts — UI animations and transitions — 0.5
- forms — *_form.dart | *-form.ts — Form state management and validation — 1
- hooks — (no dart) | use-*.ts — Reusable stateful logic (React-style) — 0.5
- directives — (no dart) | *-directive.ts — Custom DOM/element behaviors (Vue/Angular) — 0.5
- filters — (no dart) | *-filter.ts — Data formatting pipes/filters — 0.5
frontend.application:
- use_cases — *_use_case.dart | *-use-case.ts — Frontend-initiated workflows — 2
- ports — *_port.dart | *-port.ts — Interfaces for data access and external services — 0
- policies — *_policy.dart | *-policy.ts — Frontend business policies and rules — 1
- dtos — *_dto.dart | *-dto.ts — Application-internal data structures — 0
frontend.domain:
- entities — *.dart | *.ts — Domain models used on the client — 1
- value_objects — *_vo.dart | *-vo.ts — Immutable typed values — 0.5
- services — *_service.dart | *-service.ts — Pure domain logic services — 1
- specifications — *_spec.dart | *-spec.ts — Composable rules and predicates — 0.5
- exceptions — *_exception.dart | *-exception.ts — Domain-level errors — 0
frontend.integration:
- repositories — *_repository.dart | *-repository.ts — Data access implementations — 2
- clients — *_client.dart | *-client.ts — HTTP/WebSocket/GraphQL API clients — 1
- stores — *_store.dart | *-store.ts — Local persistence implementations — 1
- serializers — *_serializer.dart | *-serializer.ts — API data transformation — 0.5
- mappers — *_mapper.dart | *-mapper.ts — Data transformation between layers — 0.5
- interceptors — *_interceptor.dart | *-interceptor.ts — HTTP request/response middleware — 1
- caches — *_cache.dart | *-cache.ts — Client-side caching implementations — 0.5
- synchronizers — *_sync.dart | *-sync.ts — Offline sync and conflict resolution — 2
- monitors — *_monitor.dart | *-monitor.ts — Client-side monitoring and telemetry — 1
- validators — *_validator.dart | *-validator.ts — Client-side validation engines — 0.5
- workers — (no dart) | *.worker.ts — Background processing and web workers — 2
- connectors — *_connector.dart | *-connector.ts — Real-time and streaming connections — 1

Examples: backend.integration.engines → *_engine.py, weight 3 (highest complexity); backend.presentation.routes → *_routes.py, weight 0; frontend.presentation.controllers → *_bloc.dart / *-store.ts, weight 2.

additions.text: Suffix collisions, multi-suffix entries and TypeScript-only entries listed explicitly; no weight-aggregation formula is enforced.
additions.justification: Derived observations from the source catalog values so a verifier does not misclassify files by suffix alone, and does not enforce an aggregation formula the source never prescribes. Not a new obligation.

additions.text: Tweaking weights to shape an estimate; mixing values across entries or languages.
additions.justification: Concrete forms of the source's 'instead of inventing types or weights ad hoc' and of the per-entry, per-language catalog structure.

additions.text: side.layer.type used as the catalog lookup key (not as a prescribed URN syntax); 'flag mismatches (catalog vs coder conventions), never pick ad hoc'.
additions.justification: The lookup key mirrors the source's own example keys (S269–S271). The flag-on-mismatch move is the minimal consequence of the source's 'derived from the coder conventions' plus 'instead of inventing ... ad hoc'; no new waiver or procedure.

additions.text: fires/doesNotFire situations and activation facts, including catalog maintenance.
additions.justification: Required by target schema; derived from the source summary and statement (catalog defined, derived from coder conventions, used for derivation and estimation).

additions.text: An entry with no suffix for a language means the type is unavailable there.
additions.justification: Reading of the source catalog, where some frontend types define only a typescript suffix.

additions.text: The full catalog is delivered as new shared context node context.component-type-catalog (neutral reference data, no existing shared id fits: it is not a layer map or repo idiom but this convention's own catalog, which other planner/coder conventions may reference). The planner-specific use of it (component derivation, URN side/layer values, effort estimation) stays in this rule's given/then/prefer/why. Coder-facing text trimmed to ~1,000 characters; detail lives in evidence/verifier_detail.
additions.justification: Keeps coder-facing fields within budget while keeping rule-specific framing out of the shared node.

trace.note: Complete enumeration by side/layer/suffix/description/weight and derivation from coder conventions stated in given and at the head of the catalog node.
Weights are used for estimation; no aggregation formula is prescribed (see verifier_detail[5]).
Lineage path kept in audit and catalog node; derivation reasoning in given/prefer.
Side/layer values for component URNs come from the catalog structure; no full URN grammar is prescribed.
